ForecasterAll values: MAEnMAEDay peak at 07:00: MAEnMAEDay peak, all times: MAEnMAE
  • Forecast line. A forecast is issued every 15 minutes from 07:00 to 19:45 and always runs to 20:00. Hovering inside a shaded window shows the forecast issued at the cursor's time; it knows the load only up to the previous reading.
  • Peak forecast. The dotted line is the forecast of the window's peak: the higher of the highest load already measured since 07:00 and the forecast's own maximum plus a calibrated allowance, because a forecast line is smoother than the real load. (Persistence has no allowance.)
  • No forecast. Grey windows are low-load periods: a low-load alarm is on and the forecaster issues nothing.
  • MAE = mean absolute error in kW. nMAE = MAE ÷ mean of the actual values being compared. For a single forecast the peak figures are simply the absolute error and its share of the actual peak.
  • Circles mark each day's 07:00–20:00 peak; diamonds mark the highest of those in each calendar month of the validation period (). Times are local clock time.
